Krishna Kumar J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal by the claimant is directed against the Judgment and Award dated 17.07.2020 passed in LAC.No.1099/2018 by the I Additional District Judge, Belagavi (for short, 'the reference Court'),
whereby the said reference filed by the appellant-claimant was dismissed by the reference Court thereby confirming the award passed by the SLAO granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,73,200/-
per acre in respect of subject lands.

2. The material on record discloses that subject lands having been acquired pursuant to preliminary notification dated 23.12.2015, the appellant-claimant filed the reference under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 seeking re-determination and enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The said claim petition having been contested by the respondents, the claimant examined himself as P.W.1 and NC:
2023:KHC-D:12350-DB Ex.P.1 to 11 were marked on his behalf.
The respondents did not chose to adduce oral evidence but marked the award and the award statement as Ex.R.1 and 2 respectively.

By the impugned Judgment and Award, the reference Court proceeded to reject the reference on the ground that the said agreement dated 19.12.2014 marked at Ex.P.1 and sale deed dated 23.02.2015 marked as Ex.P.2 by the claimant, in respect of Kadrolli village which were far away from the subject lands and consequently, no reliance can be placed upon the said documents particularly when documents in respect of Budihal village where subject lands were situated had not been produced by the appellant-claimant before the reference Court.

In this context, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that if one more opportunity is provided, the claimant would produce additional oral and documentary evidence in support of his claim for enhancement of compensation including documents relating to Budihal village/or nearby villages for the purpose of enabling appellant-claimant to seek higher compensation which is permissible under Section 26 of the said Act, 2013.

It is therefore submitted that the impugned Judgment and Award passed by the reference Court be set NC: 2023:KHC-D:12350-DB aside and the matter may be remitted back to the Sri Mahadev S/O. Nagappa Suryavanshi vs The Spl.Land Acquisition Officer on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181699793/
2 reference Court for reconsideration afresh by providing one more opportunity in favour of the appellant-claimant to adduce additional evidence in support of his claim.
3.

Per Contra, learned counsel for the respondents would support the impugned Judgment and Award and submit that there is no merit in the appeal and same is liable to be dismissed.
4.

A perusal of the impugned Judgment and Award will indicate that though the appellant had produced sale agreement at Ex.P.1 and sale deed Ex.P.2 in relation to the lands at Kadrolli, the reference Court has refused to accept the same on the ground that said village was situated far away from the subject lands situated at Budihal.
As stated supra, the appellant contends that the subject lands situated at Budihal are situated in the same vicinity as the lands covered under Ex.P.1 and 2.

Further, in the light of the specific assertion on the part of the appellant that if one more opportunity is provided, appellant would produce additional evidence in relation to the lands situated at Budihal/or other neighbouring villages also, in order to provide one more opportunity in favour NC: 2023:KHC-D:12350-DB of the appellant to substantiate his claim, we deem it just and appropriate to set aside the impugned Judgment and Award and remit the matter back to the reference Court for reconsideration afresh in accordance with law.

In the result, we pass the following :
ORDER (i) Appeal is hereby allowed.

(ii) The impugned Judgment and Award dated 17.07.2020 passed in LAC.No.1099/2018 by the I Additional District Judge, Belagavi is hereby set aside and the matter is remitted back to the reference Court for reconsideration afresh in accordance with law.
(iii) Parties undertake to appear before the reference Court on 06.11.2023 without awaiting further notice from the reference Court.
(iv) Liberty is reserved in favour of the parties to adduce additional oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective claims.
(v) The reference Court is directed to dispose of the reference proceedings within a period of three months from 06.11.2022.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12350-DB (vi) The registry is directed to refund back the entire (100%) Court fee paid in this appeal back to the appellant forthwith without any delay.

Sd/-
